Rink markings as a data frame

Source: R/rink_geometry.R
rink_geometry.Rd

Returns every rink marking as tidy coordinates: one row per vertex, grouped by shape. This is what annotate_rink() draws, exposed so you can reuse the geometry elsewhere (another plotting library, an interactive map, a point-in-zone test, ...). Markings are listed in drawing order (bottom to top).

Usage

rink_geometry(dimensions = IIHF, details = FALSE, slot = FALSE)

Arguments

dimensions

Rink dimensions, e.g. IIHF or NHL (see rink_dims).

details

If TRUE, include the faceoff-circle hash marks and the cut-outs inside the faceoff dots.

slot

If TRUE, include the offensive-zone slot (the high-danger area in front of the right-hand goal).

Value

A data frame with columns:

shape

Marking name, e.g. "centre_circle", "blue_line_left".

group

Integer id, unique per shape, in drawing order.

kind

"polygon" (closed) or "path" (open line).

x, y

Vertex coordinates, in the frame of dimensions.

colour, fill

Style roles: "line" (the marking colour), "ice" (the rink fill colour), "slot" (the slot styling) or NA (none).

linewidth

"small", "big", "slot" or NA (the ggplot2 default).

alpha

Fill alpha (NA for the slot, which takes slot_alpha in annotate_rink()).

linejoin

Line-join style for the outline.

See also

annotate_rink()

Examples

geo <- rink_geometry(IIHF)
unique(geo$shape)
#>  [1] "ice"                "centre_circle"      "centre_dot"        
#>  [4] "faceoff_dot_lb"     "faceoff_circle_lb"  "faceoff_dot_lt"    
#>  [7] "faceoff_circle_lt"  "faceoff_dot_rb"     "faceoff_circle_rb" 
#> [10] "faceoff_dot_rt"     "faceoff_circle_rt"  "nz_dot_lb"         
#> [13] "nz_dot_lt"          "nz_dot_rb"          "nz_dot_rt"         
#> [16] "goal_right"         "goal_left"          "centre_line_bottom"
#> [19] "centre_line_top"    "blue_line_left"     "blue_line_right"   
#> [22] "goal_line_left"     "goal_line_right"    "crease_left_fill"  
#> [25] "crease_left"        "crease_right_fill"  "crease_right"      
#> [28] "boards"            

# Draw it yourself
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(geo[geo$kind == "path", ], aes(x, y, group = group)) +
  geom_path() +
  coord_fixed()
